days.label: Bhagavad Gita 1.1 to 1.47
days.key: Having thus spoken on the battle-field, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow, his mind overborne by grief.
days.s: Closing the chapter, Sanjaya reports how Arjuna ends his plea against slaying his kinsmen; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 1.47, reads his collapse as moved by affection for kin, pity and fear that right would suffer, though the other side had often plotted his death.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 1.47, archive.org gita-bhasya (A. Govindacharya’s translation, 1898)

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 2.1 to 2.72
days.key: Nor at any time verily was I not, nor thou, nor these princes of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be, hereafter.
days.s: Krishna, answering Arjuna, who has said he will not fight and fallen silent, begins to teach why the wise do not grieve; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 2.12, takes the plural to mean the many bodies, not many selves, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 2.12, as teaching that souls are many and distinct from God.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 2.12, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri (1901), archive.org; Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 2.12, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898), archive.org

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 3.1 to 3.43
days.key: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.
days.s: Having named desire as the foe that drives a man to sin, Krishna, near the chapter’s close, ranks the powers within; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 3.42, reads the closing ‘He’ as the Self, the witness of reason, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 3.42, as desire, strongest and most overpowering of all.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri (1901); Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898); both archive.org

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 4.1 to 4.42
days.key: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.
days.s: Having likened wisdom to a raft across all sin, Krishna gives Arjuna a second image; Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 4.37, reads it as wisdom making actions powerless, not literally burning them, while those that brought this body into being must still run their course.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 4.37, trans. A. Mahadeva Sastri, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 5.1 to 5.29
days.key: Sages look equally on a Brâhmana adorned with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.
days.s: Krishna, having spoken of wisdom that destroys unwisdom, turns to how the wise regard beings of every rank; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 5.18, reads it as seeing every self as equal, alike in intelligence, with differences of form belonging to matter, not spirit.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 5.18, trans. A. Govindacharya (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 6.1 to 6.47
days.key: As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogî of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the Self.
days.s: Between rules for sitting and eating and an account of yoga’s joy, Krishna gives an image; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 6.19, reads the flame as the yogi’s self, shining steady in its light of knowledge once the mind’s distractions are shut out.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, 6.19, A. Govindacharya’s translation, archive.org gita-bhasya (1898)

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 7.1 to 7.30
days.key: There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string.
days.s: Having named his two natures as the womb of all beings, Krishna speaks to Arjuna of his own place; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 7.7, reads the string as a soul holding its body together: all things, sentient and insentient, are the body that Krishna ensouls.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 7.7, archive.org gita-bhasya (A. Govindacharya’s translation, 1898)

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 8.1 to 8.28
days.key: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî.
days.s: After the yogi who departs uttering Aum, Krishna turns to the devotee of unbroken remembrance; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 8.14, reads that ease as Krishna’s own work: unable to bear parting from such a devotee, he chooses him, ripens his meditation and clears its obstacles.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 8.14, A. Govindacharya’s English translation (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 9.1 to 9.34
days.key: He who offereth to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that I accept from the striving self, offered as it is with devotion.
days.s: Having set heavens won by ritual against his worshippers’ goal, Krishna turns to humble gifts; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 9.26, reads it as Krishna, wanting nothing and ever in bliss, still relishing such a gift as if newly given a delight beyond hope.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 9.26, trans. A. Govindacharya (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 10.1 to 10.42
days.key: I, O Gudakesha, am the Self, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.
days.s: Granting Arjuna’s plea for his glories, Krishna names this first, ahead of the chief of each kind; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 10.20, reads it as the Lord seated as soul in beings who form his body, and so their support, ruler and master.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 10.20, A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 11.1 to 11.55
days.key: Time am I, laying desolate the world, Made manifest on earth to slay mankind!
days.s: Asked by Arjuna who the devouring form is, Krishna declares the opposing warriors doomed and bids him fight; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 11.32, takes Time from a root meaning to count: the one who reckons when the life-span of each king ranged against Arjuna runs out.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, 11.32, in A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 12.1 to 12.20
days.key: The difficulty of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifested is greater; for the path of the Unmanifested is hard for the embodied to reach.
days.s: Krishna calls devotees fixed on him best in yoga, though worshippers of the Imperishable reach him too; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 12.5, reads the Unmanifested as the Imperishable Supreme Reality, hard to reach because attachment to the body must be abandoned, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 12.5, as the individual soul, reached only with great struggle.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 12.5, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri (1901); Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 12.5, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898); archive.org (OCR)

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 13.1 to 13.34
days.key: Understand Me as the Knower of the Field in all Fields, O Bhârata.
days.s: Answering Arjuna’s question on matter and spirit, Krishna calls the body the field, then speaks of himself; Śaṅkara, on 13.2, reads it as the knower in every body being the Lord, whom the round of births, resting only on ignorance, never touches.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya on 13.2, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 14.1 to 14.27
days.key: And he who serveth Me exclusively by the Yoga of devotion, he, crossing beyond the qualities, he is fit to become the Eternal.
days.s: Krishna answers the last part of Arjuna’s question, how to cross the three qualities; Madhva (Dvaita), on 14.26, takes Brahman, the verse’s ‘Eternal’, as the intelligent Prakriti, so that fitness for it means being as beloved of the Lord as that Prakriti is.
days.src: Madhva, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 14.26, in S. Subba Rau’s translation (1906), archive.org india.history.resource.91865

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 15.1 to 15.20
days.key: A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit, draweth round itself the senses of which the mind is the sixth, veiled in matter.
days.s: Having named his supreme abode, from which none return, Krishna turns to the embodied soul; Śaṅkara (Advaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 15.7, reads this portion as a portion only in imagination, like the sun’s reflection in water, which returns to the sun once the water is removed.
days.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 15.7, trans. A. Mahadeva Sastri, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 16.1 to 16.24
days.key: Therefore let the Scriptures be thy authority, in determining what ought to be done, or what ought not to be done. Knowing what hath been declared by the ordinances of the Scriptures, thou oughtest to work in this world.
days.s: Closing the chapter on two natures, Krishna turns from those who follow desire to a charge for Arjuna; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 16.24, reads the scriptures as teaching the truth of the Supreme Person and enjoining works that please him and lead to him.
days.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 16.24, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 17.1 to 17.28
days.key: The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith; that which his faith is, he is even that.
days.s: Answering Arjuna’s question about worship in faith without the scriptures’ ordinances, Krishna begins to sort faith into three kinds; Madhva (Dvaita), on 17.3, reads faith as following the soul’s essential nature, so that pure faith marks the soul itself as pure.
days.src: Madhva, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 17.3, tr. S. Subba Rau (1906), archive.org india.history.resource.91865

days.label: Bhagavad Gita 18.1 to 18.78
days.key: Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.
days.s: Krishna, after promising Arjuna his supreme word, most secret of all, speaks it; Madhva (Dvaita), on 18.66, reads the abandoning as giving up the fruits of duty and any duty not done to please the Lord, since Krishna could not otherwise urge Arjuna to fight, and Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 18.66, as renouncing all works, unrighteous as well as righteous.
days.src: Madhva, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 18.66, tr. S. Subba Rau (1906); Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 18.66, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri, 2nd ed. (1901); both archive.org
